operator_io_quirks: Mixed-case identifiers everywhere (County_Id, Party_ID, Lieutenant_Governor, US_Senate); must double-quote in generated SQL.
Table 'party' has a column also named 'Party' (same name as table) and 'election' has column 'Party' that is an FK to party.Party_ID — name collision between table and column.
Column 'Year' declared REAL but semantically a year; ts_fuzzer dispatches to Number (not Date) because type_str is 'real'.
Column 'First_Elected' declared REAL, holds years (1994..2006); Number fuzzer will produce floats in [-10^4,10^4] — implausible years.
Column 'Zip_code' declared TEXT but values are district codes 'D21','D08' — String fuzzer will not reproduce the D-prefix pattern.
Column 'Counties_Represented' TEXT with values like '09.1 9A','12.1 12A' — space-separated multi-token strings; String fuzzer treats as opaque.
Column 'Delegate' TEXT with comma+period names 'Bates, Gail H. Gail H. Bates' — long strings, String length range will be [min,max+1] of these.
Column 'US_Senate' contains literal '(no election)' — a sentinel string; String fuzzer may contaminate it.
All tables tiny (county=5, party=7, election=8 rows); original_values sampling k=min(5,len) will use nearly all rows.
FK election.District -> county.County_Id and election.Party -> party.Party_ID both parent_exists=true, non-null parents, unique PKs — clean FKs.
No NOT NULL, no CHECK, no UNIQUE constraints beyond PKs; no views/triggers/indexes in DDL.
All columns null_rate=0.0 in original; TS may still emit NULLs via FK-empty-parent path or String/Number dropout.
operator_ts_expectations: Number fuzzer on County_Id/Party_ID/Election_ID (INT PKs): range [-10^4,10^4], int perturbation +-1/+-2; PK dedup keeps first occurrence, so sizes shrink toward distinct count.
Number fuzzer on Population (REAL): floats in [-10^4,10^4] — plausible magnitude but sign/decimals implausible vs 13300..90000.
Number fuzzer on Year/First_Elected (REAL): floats in [-10^4,10^4] — will produce negative years and non-integer years; drives FN on year-range predicates.
String fuzzer on County_name/Party/Governor/etc: random a-zA-Z0-9() strings length [min,max+1] of originals, plus 50% contaminate — implausible names, drives FN on equality/IN predicates.
String fuzzer on Zip_code: random strings, loses 'D' prefix pattern — FN on LIKE 'D%' style predicates.
String fuzzer on Counties_Represented: random strings, loses 'NN.N NX' multi-token structure — FN on string-split predicates.
FK election.Party draws from party.Party_ID final values; FK election.District draws from county.County_Id final values — ties preserved, so joins work.
Table sizes: choose_table_sizes gives ~30-230 rows per table (rand_lin) or level-based 1+30u then x4 capped 2500 — much larger than originals (5-8), so many duplicate non-PK values.
PK dedup on tiny tables: county/party/election PKs are INT with range 2*10^4, so ~all rows survive dedup; sizes stay near chosen n.
No unique non-PK columns, so drop_unique_duplicates is a no-op here.

Missing ties/duplicates: original has distinct=4-8 per column; TS generates many rows with repeated String values (from element pool) — may create ties the original lacks (FP on GROUP BY / DISTINCT predicates).
Implausible values (negative years, random names) drive FN on range/equality predicates; missing sentinel '(no election)' and 'D'-prefix codes drive FN on pattern predicates.
